title: Python tutorial, 4.9.1 Default Argument Values
summary: States that a default value is evaluated only once, which matters when the default is a mutable object such as a list or dictionary. Shows the fix of using None as the default and creating the list inside the function.
keywords: mutable default argument list dict evaluated once None

title: CPython issue 26842: tutorial should explain default parameter lifetime
summary: A public report asking the tutorial to explain how long default parameter values live. It was closed as won't fix, so the tutorial keeps its short warning.
keywords: mutable default argument parameter lifetime list shared calls

title: Python tutorial, 4.2 for Statements
summary: Says that code which modifies a collection while iterating over it can be tricky to get right, and that it is usually more straightforward to loop over a copy or to build a new collection.
keywords: modify list while iterating loop copy new collection remove

title: Python Programming FAQ: why do lambdas defined in a loop all return the same result
summary: Explains that functions created in a loop read the loop variable when they are called, so they all return the same result. Recommends binding the current value with a default argument, such as lambda n=x: n**2.
keywords: closure lambda loop variable late binding default argument

title: CPython issue 13094: need Programming FAQ entry for the behavior of closures
summary: A public report asking for a Programming FAQ entry that explains how closures behave.
keywords: closure lambda loop variable behavior faq
